texts.story: You rented Mr Tan's flat for 12 months and paid a $2,600 deposit on 3 Aug 2025. You moved out on 31 Jul 2026 and he wrote "ok, all good". On 15 Aug he refused to return the deposit, saying the sofa was damaged.
texts.summary: I rented the Respondent's flat at Blk 123 Bedok North Street 1 #05-67 from 3 Aug 2025 for 12 months and paid a $2,600 deposit on 3 Aug 2025. Clause 4 of the tenancy agreement says the deposit is refunded within 14 days of moving out, less damage. I moved out on 31 Jul 2026. The Respondent wrote "ok, all good" the same day. On 15 Aug 2026 he refused to return the deposit, saying the sofa was scratched, and sent no photo or invoice. I claim the $2,600 deposit.
texts.written_request:
Dear Mr Tan,

I am writing about the deposit of $2,600 that I paid on 3 August 2025 for the flat at Blk 123 Bedok North Street 1 #05-67.

Clause 4 of our tenancy agreement says the deposit is refunded within 14 days after I move out, less the cost of repairing any damage beyond fair wear and tear. I moved out on 31 July 2026 and you wrote "ok, all good" the same day. The refund was due on 14 August 2026.

On 15 August you said the sofa has a scratch and that the deposit cannot be returned. I have asked twice for a photo. None has been sent.

Please return the $2,600 to my bank account within 7 days of this letter, by [date]. If you say any part should be held back, please send me a photo of the damage, a repair invoice or quote, and the amount you are holding back, so I can consider it.

If I do not hear from you by then, I will file a claim at the Small Claims Tribunals.

Yours sincerely,
Mei Ling
